name: Downtown Mobile
geoReference: Central business and riverfront historic core bounded roughly by the Mobile River (east), Broad Street (west), Beauregard St / Three Mile Creek fringe (north), and I-10 / Canal St (south); corridors include Dauphin St, Government St (US-90), Royal St, and Water St.
pickupNotes: Inside City of Mobile limits. Multi-story offices, historic commercial storefronts, freight elevators, alleys, and metered street loading require advance coordination.
description: Central business and historic riverfront district encompassing Lower Dauphin Street, Church Street East, De Tonti Square edge, and the Downtown Mobile BID.
notes: Inside City of Mobile limits. Requires 2+ first-party local evidence items before publishing dedicated neighborhood page.

name: Midtown Mobile
geoReference: Historic oak-lined residential and commercial belt west of Broad Street and east of I-65 along Dauphin St, Old Shell Rd, Spring Hill Ave, Government St (US-90), and Airport Blvd.
pickupNotes: Inside City of Mobile limits. Historic bungalows, narrow shared driveways, detached carriage houses/garages, and street-canopy clearance considerations.
description: Broad everyday Mobile area name between Broad Street and I-65 encompassing the NRHP-listed Midtown Historic District, Old Dauphin Way, Leinkauf, and Ashland Place.
notes: Classified as local-area-name spanning multiple official historic districts inside Mobile.

name: West Mobile
geoReference: Suburban Mobile west of I-65 along Airport Blvd, Cottage Hill Rd, Hillcrest Rd, University Blvd, Cody Rd, Schillinger Rd, Zeigler Blvd, Grelot Rd, and Dawes Rd.
pickupNotes: Spans both western City of Mobile corporate limits (active coverage) and adjacent unincorporated Mobile County subdivisions beyond city limits (confirm address before scheduling).
description: Widely used regional name ('WeMo') for suburban areas west of I-65; no single official GIS polygon, spanning western Mobile city limits and unincorporated subdivisions.
notes: In-city West Mobile addresses are active; unincorporated western 36695/36608 subdivisions confirmed by street address.

name: Spring Hill
geoReference: Hilltop residential community (~6 miles west of Downtown) along Old Shell Rd, Spring Hill Ave, and McGregor Ave west of I-65; home to Spring Hill College and Langan Park (4851 Museum Dr recycling center).
pickupNotes: Inside City of Mobile limits. Mix of historic estates, long wooded driveways, two-story residences, and student/faculty housing.
description: Historic hilltop community west of I-65 containing the NRHP-listed Spring Hill Historic District, Spring Hill College, and Municipal/Langan Park.

name: Oakleigh Garden District
geoReference: MHDC Local ARB and NRHP historic district south of Government Street (US-90) centered around Washington Square between Broad/Marine Streets and Rapier/Ann Streets.
pickupNotes: Inside City of Mobile limits. Narrow historic streets, on-street parking, raised cottages, and architectural review district preservation sensitivity.
description: Official MHDC Architectural Review Board and National Register historic district (listed 1972) centered around Washington Square and Historic Oakleigh House.

name: Crichton
geoReference: Northwest of Midtown and east of I-65 along Spring Hill Avenue (US-98) and Mobile Street near Three Mile Creek.
pickupNotes: Inside City of Mobile limits; mix of residential lots and light commercial/industrial properties along Spring Hill Ave and Mobile St.
description: Historic community (North Crichton and South Crichton) annexed into the City of Mobile along the Spring Hill Avenue corridor.

name: Toulminville
geoReference: Northwest of Downtown along St. Stephens Road (US-45), Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Avenue, and Gorgas Street south of the Prichard municipal line.
pickupNotes: Inside City of Mobile limits; verify northern border addresses near Prichard line.
description: Historic 1830s settlement annexed into Mobile in the 1940s along St. Stephens Road (US-45) and MLK Jr. Avenue.

name: Maysville
geoReference: NRHP-listed Maysville Historic District south of Leinkauf; roughly bounded by Virginia Street (north), South Ann Street (east), Duval Street (south), and Houston Street (west).
pickupNotes: Inside City of Mobile limits.
description: Official 451-acre National Register historic district (NRHP #13000959) southwest of Downtown and directly south of Leinkauf.
notes: Official NRHP district mapped in MHDC GIS.

name: Oakdale
geoReference: NRHP-listed Oakdale Historic District south of Downtown/Oakleigh and east of Maysville; roughly bounded by Virginia St / I-10 (north), I-10 / S. Broad St (east), Preston Ave (south), and S. Ann St (west).
pickupNotes: Inside City of Mobile limits.
description: Official National Register streetcar-era historic district (NRHP #14001005) south of Oakleigh and east of Maysville.
notes: Official NRHP district mapped in MHDC GIS.

name: Dog River
geoReference: South Mobile tidal river watershed and waterfront residential/marina corridor along AL-163 (Dauphin Island Pkwy / Dog River Bridge), Dog River Dr, Riviere du Chien Rd, and Halls Mill Rd.
pickupNotes: Spans southern City of Mobile limits and unincorporated Dog River waterfront pockets; elevated waterfront homes, boathouses, and long sloped drives.
description: Waterfront residential and marina community surrounding the tidal Dog River watershed in south Mobile.
notes: Verify parcel city-limit status when scheduling southern shore addresses.

name: Africatown (Plateau)
geoReference: Approximately 3 miles north of Downtown on the west bank of the Mobile River north of Three Mile Creek along US-90/98 (Cochrane-Africatown USA Bridge / Bay Bridge Rd), US-43 (Telegraph Rd), and I-165.
pickupNotes: Primarily inside City of Mobile corporate limits (including the NRHP Africatown Historic District), with northern/western margins abutting the City of Prichard.
description: Historic community (also known as Plateau and Magazine Point) founded in 1866 by Clotilda survivors; encompasses the NRHP-listed Africatown Historic District (#12000990) and City of Mobile Africatown Neighborhood Plan.
notes: Priority Mobile community record from Phase 2 GIS research.

name: Peninsula
geoReference: South Mobile coastal peninsula bounded by I-10 (north), Mobile Bay and Brookley Aeroplex (east), and Dog River / Perch Creek (south and west) along the 5-mile spine of AL-163 (Dauphin Island Pkwy).
pickupNotes: Inside City of Mobile limits; includes the City Recycling Drop-Off Center at 1750 Dauphin Island Pkwy.
description: Distinct south Mobile coastal peninsula defined by The Peninsula of Mobile Corridor Master Plan between I-10, Mobile Bay, and Dog River.
notes: Priority Mobile community record from Phase 2 GIS research.

name: De Tonti Square
geoReference: Immediately north of Downtown Mobile's business core between Beauregard/Adams Streets (north), N. Jackson/Claiborne Streets (east), St. Louis/St. Anthony Streets (south), and N. Conception/Joachim Streets (west).
pickupNotes: Inside City of Mobile limits; historic townhomes and commercial offices with tight street parking.
description: Official MHDC Local ARB and NRHP historic district (listed 1972) immediately north of Downtown's central business core.

name: Church Street East
geoReference: Downtown Mobile historic civic/residential district along Church Street, Government Street, and Conti/Monroe Streets between Royal/Water Streets and Broad/Washington Ave.
pickupNotes: Inside City of Mobile limits.
description: Official MHDC Local ARB and NRHP historic district (listed 1971) in Downtown Mobile.

name: Old Dauphin Way
geoReference: Bisected by Dauphin Street between Spring Hill Avenue (north), Broad Street (east), Government Street (south), and Houston Street (west).
pickupNotes: Inside City of Mobile limits; Mobile's largest local historic district (~766 acres) with narrow driveways and mature live oaks.
description: Official MHDC Local ARB and NRHP historic district (~766 acres) bisected by Dauphin Street.

name: Leinkauf
geoReference: Immediately south of Government Street (north of Maysville) around Monterey St, Lamar St, Michigan Ave, and Virginia St.
pickupNotes: Inside City of Mobile limits.
description: Official MHDC Local ARB and NRHP historic district south of Government Street.

name: Ashland Place
geoReference: Midtown Mobile along Ashland Place Avenue, Lanier Ave, and Ryan Ave between Old Shell Road and Spring Hill Avenue.
pickupNotes: Inside City of Mobile limits.
description: Official MHDC Local ARB and NRHP early-20th-century residential historic district in Midtown Mobile.

name: Campground
geoReference: Northwest of Downtown and north of Old Dauphin Way between Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Avenue (north), Ann Street (east), St. Stephens Rd / Spring Hill Ave (south), and Rylands Street (west).
pickupNotes: Inside City of Mobile limits.
description: NRHP-listed Campground Historic District (listed 2005) northwest of Downtown Mobile.

name: Cottage Hill
geoReference: Major residential and commercial corridor along Cottage Hill Road west of I-65 across Azalea Rd, University Blvd, Hillcrest Rd (Medal of Honor Park), Cody Rd, and Schillinger Rd.
pickupNotes: Primarily inside City of Mobile limits east of Schillinger Rd, with westernmost subdivisions extending into unincorporated Mobile County.
description: Commonly used corridor and neighborhood area name centered along Cottage Hill Road in Southwest/West Mobile.

name: Hillsdale
geoReference: West Mobile north of Zeigler Blvd and the University of South Alabama campus between Cody Rd N and Overlook Rd around Hillsdale Park (558 E. Felhorn Rd).
pickupNotes: Inside City of Mobile limits.
description: Established post-WWII planned residential community in West Mobile inside Mobile city limits.
